name: totem

attributes.attribute: an animal or plant believed to be tribal ancestor
tribe forbidden to kill or eat the onetime relative
regarded as ancestors by some coastal Irish families
forbidden to kill birds because his mother descended from them

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The totem is a cosmological concept. Scholars use the word for an animal, and sometimes a plant, that a tribe thought of as its ancient source. This old bond brought a rule. The tribe could not kill or eat the flesh of that relative. Traces of such a folk belief remain. Some coastal Irish families claim they come from Seal women. In one tale, the king Conaire could not kill birds because his mother was of their line.

okr.objective: Record the Celtic concept of the totem.
key_results: A totem is an animal, or plant, seen as the ancestor of a tribe
The tribe could not kill or eat its onetime relative
Some Irish families traced descent from Seal women
King Conaire could not kill birds because his mother came from them
